I am seventy years old and my legs are not what they used to be, so I keep my land simple. Here in Quzhou, the soil is good for wheat and maize in rotation — that is what I have done my whole life, and I see no reason to change now. I have about nine mu in total. I will plant wheat on seven mu this autumn after the rains; it sleeps through the winter and I harvest it in June. Right after that, I put maize into the same ground without ploughing — I just plant into the wheat stubble like everyone else now, it saves diesel and my back. For wheat, I buy improved seeds from the township store and spread compound fertilizer as base dressing, then top up with urea when the weather warms in spring. The maize gets hybrid seed, mostly Denghai or something similar the dealer recommends, and I do not bother with much extra fertilizer for it because the wheat already fed the soil. I still keep two mu of cotton because the cash is useful for medicine and daily costs, even though at my age the spraying is hard — cotton needs spraying every few days against bollworm and aphids. I irrigate from my well: wheat four times, maize three times, and cotton four times, mostly in the hot months. I hire a young neighbor to help with the cotton spraying and the harvest, because my hands shake now and I cannot carry the tank anymore. I till the wheat and cotton plots with the rotary tiller, but the maize is no-till.
